summary: For p≥5 inert in the unramified quadratic local datum with π=−p, plan the two-variable norm-compatible unit module, inverse Tate twist, anticyclotomic quotient, Coleman character derivatives and signed formal Kummer duality. Construct the independent optimal plus unit and formal-CM optimal local-point system, then prove integral Rubin decomposition and nonzero correct-parity generator derivatives. General Lubin–Tate geometry, completed algebras, CM special values and finite-field counts are imported under precise contracts.

nodes.title: Anticyclotomic conductor parity
nodes.statement: For finite continuous χ:G⁻→Q̄_p×, define c(1)=0 and c(χ)=n+1 when Φ_n is its first Lubin–Tate level. Put Ξ⁺={χ:c(χ) even}, Ξ⁻={χ:c(χ) odd}. For a nontrivial character of exact order p^n on Gal(Ψ_n/Φ), c(χ)=n+1; the trivial character belongs to Ξ⁺.
hypotheses: The standing BKO local datum: p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, O=O_Φ, π=−p, a Lubin–Tate O-module F for π, and the specified π-adic Tate basis and towers.
proofSteps: Use the conductor and quotient identifications supplied by LT.8/bko-character-data.
Assign parity to the conductor exponent; include the trivial character separately.

sources.locator: §2, p.948 (conductor convention) and p.949 (definition of Ξ⁺, Ξ⁻)
sources.match: BKO assign conductor p^(n+1) to a nontrivial anticyclotomic character whose first level of factorization is Gal(Φ_n/Φ), and conductor 1 to the trivial character; on p.949 they put a character in Ξ⁺ or Ξ⁻ according as its conductor is an even or an odd power of p. The node records this exponent and parity; since Gal(Ψ_n/Φ) is cyclic of order p^n, exact order p^n gives exponent n+1.

nodes.title: Norm-compatible principal units
nodes.statement: Let P_n be TauCeti.unitFiltration Φ_n 1, written additively via p-adic powering. Define Ũ_∞=lim_N(P_n⊗_{Z_p}O), with its compact inverse-limit topology and O[[Δ×Γ]] action. Let U_∞=e_ω Ũ_∞, where ω is the tame restriction of κ and e_ω=|Δ|⁻¹Σ ω(d)⁻¹d; Γ=G⁺×G⁻ and Λ₂=O[[Γ]].
hypotheses: The standing BKO local datum: p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, O=O_Φ, π=−p, a Lubin–Tate O-module F for π, and the specified π-adic Tate basis and towers.
proofSteps: Use the existing principal-unit group, finite norm maps and p-adic module structure.
Extend norms by O and form the closed compatible-family submodule; extend the continuous Galois action to the completed algebra.
Apply the prime-to-p idempotent and retain its embedding and projection.

sources.match: BKO take U_n to be the principal units of Φ_n, form the norm inverse limit of U_n⊗_(Z_p)O, and define U_∞ as the part on which Δ acts through ω. The node realises U_n as Tau Ceti's depth-one unit filtration and writes the ω-part with the explicit idempotent.
Rubin makes the same definition, with Λ₂=O[[Gal(Φ_∞/Φ₀)]] acting on the ω-part of the norm limit.

acceptance: Use the existing principal-unit filtration at every coordinate, and reject a family failing one norm square.

nodes.title: Inverse Tate twist
nodes.statement: For a compact O-module M with compatible Galois action, set M*=Hom_O(T_πF,M) with g·h=g_M∘h∘g_T⁻¹ and the compact topology after choosing a Tate basis. Define U_∞*=(Ũ_∞*)^Δ; evaluation at a basis identifies it with U_∞ and changes the Γ-action by κ⁻¹. This is a functorial comparison, not an identification of the original Γ-actions.
hypotheses: The standing BKO local datum: p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, O=O_Φ, π=−p, a Lubin–Tate O-module F for π, and the specified π-adic Tate basis and towers.
proofSteps: Import the actual rank-one Tate O-module and κ.
Use the contragredient action on Hom, then identify Δ-invariants with the ω-summand through evaluation.
Prove change of basis by b∈O× rescales evaluation and inverse-basis tensors by inverse factors.

The node adds the basis-change and functoriality bookkeeping.

acceptance: The κ-line becomes trivial after inverse twisting; the resulting tame invariant corresponds to ω, not ω⁻¹.

nodes.title: Anticyclotomic local-unit quotient
nodes.statement: For a topological generator σ of G⁺, put V_∞=U_∞/(σ−κ(σ))U_∞ and V_∞*=U_∞*/(σ−1)U_∞*. The images are compact and closed. The twist gives (V_∞)*≃V_∞* as Λ=O[[G⁻]] modules; replacing σ by another generator gives the same closed relation ideal.
hypotheses: The standing BKO local datum: p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, O=O_Φ, π=−p, a Lubin–Tate O-module F for π, and the specified π-adic Tate basis and towers.
proofSteps: Extend γ↦κ(γ)⁻¹γ to the completed algebra.
Use its automorphism to compare the two relation submodules.
Use the universal quotient property and the unit-exponent identity to show independence of σ.

nodes.title: Two-variable local-unit freeness
nodes.statement: U_∞ is free of rank two over Λ₂. Consequently U_∞* is free of rank two over the twisted Λ₂, and V_∞* is free of rank two over Λ.
hypotheses: The standing BKO local datum: p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, O=O_Φ, π=−p, a Lubin–Tate O-module F for π, and the specified π-adic Tate basis and towers.
proofSteps: Apply Wintenberger §4 Theorem (i),(iii) for r=2, K=Φ, d=2: the ω-isotypic character is nontrivial and is distinct from the tame cyclotomic character ω^(p+1).

Use the local Artin interpretation and finite coinvariant freeness in §5.1–§5.5.3; the relevant character avoids both the valuation summand and the cyclotomic Tate summand. Extend coefficients to O and select ω.
Transport freeness through the twist automorphism and specialize the G⁺ variable at 1.

sources.match: Rubin states that U_∞ is free of rank two over Λ₂ and V_∞ free of rank two over Λ, deriving the first from Wintenberger and the second from it; BKO §2, p.948, repeats both facts.

For an abelian tower with Galois group a prime-to-p group times Z_p², Wintenberger proves that the component of the completed multiplicative limit attached to a tame character is free of rank [K:Q_p], for every tame character other than the one through which the tame group acts on p-th roots of unity, and that away from the trivial character this component equals the principal-unit limit. With ω different from 1 and from ω^(p+1) this gives the node.

acceptance: Show why ω is different from the tame cyclotomic character; do not assume the exceptional character component is free.
Exhibit a Λ-module equivalence V_∞*≃Λ², including the quotient topology.

nodes.title: Lubin–Tate Coleman series
nodes.statement: For each norm-compatible u_n∈1+m_(Φ_n) and genuine basis v=(v_n) of T_πF with [π]v_(n+1)=v_n, there is a unique f_(u,v)∈O[[X]]× satisfying f_(u,v)(v_n)=u_n for all n≥0. It is fixed by the Coleman norm N_F defined by (N_F f)([π]X)=∏_{t∈F[π]}f(X+_F t). Extend its logarithmic derivative O-linearly to the tensor unit module; do not interpret a general tensor as a single multiplicative sequence.
hypotheses: The standing BKO local datum: p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, O=O_Φ, π=−p, a Lubin–Tate O-module F for π, and the specified π-adic Tate basis and towers.
proofSteps: Apply the parent finite-free determinant norm to the finite flat [π] substitution algebra, using the imported LT division polynomial and analytic evaluation.
Prove integral norm contraction, construct the norm-fixed limit from finite interpolation, and prove uniqueness by torsion evaluations accumulating at the boundary and the norm-fixed constraint.
Check the actual π-adic basis against the p-adic basis: Rubin coordinates differ by (−1)^n.

sources.match: BKO take for each norm-compatible u the Coleman power series f in O[[X]]× with f(v_n)=u_n, for a generator v of the π-adic Tate module, and footnote 2 warns that Coleman's theory fails for the p-adic Tate generator Rubin used. Coleman's existence, uniqueness and norm-fixedness are cited, not proved; the node states them for the π-basis.
Rubin quotes Coleman's interpolation theorem for norm-compatible units, with the p-adic generator corrected in source issue E4.

acceptance: Establish the stated integral assertion with all standing conventions and the listed comparison maps.

proofSteps: Use dlog(fg)=dlog f+dlog g and the invariant derivation D=λ′(X)⁻¹d/dX.
Check balancing and rescaling from the Coleman basis-change law and λ([b]X)=bλ(X).
Prove δ integral and finite evaluations continuous, and compare formal differentiation with PowerSeries.derivative.

nodes.title: Twisted derivative covariance
nodes.statement: For x∈U_∞*, β∈Gal(Φ_∞/Φ) and n≥0, δ_n(βx)=β(δ_n(x)). Before the inverse twist the formula includes κ(β); twisting cancels exactly that factor. On G⁺-coinvariants the descended δ satisfies δ(λx)=aug(λ)δ(x) for λ∈Λ.
hypotheses: The standing BKO local datum: p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, O=O_Φ, π=−p, a Lubin–Tate O-module F for π, and the specified π-adic Tate basis and towers.
proofSteps: Compare the Coleman series of βu with substitution by [κ(β)] and use the invariant differential chain rule.
Cancel the Tate factor and evaluate at zero and v_n.
Extend from group elements to the completed group algebra using continuity.

sources.match: BKO state δ_n(γx)=δ_n(x)^γ for γ∈Gal(Φ_∞/Φ) on the twisted module.
Before twisting, Rubin's δ_n(u^γ)=κ(γ)δ_n(u)^γ; the inverse twist cancels the factor κ(γ), and at the origin it gives augmentation-linearity of δ.

nodes.title: Character derivatives
nodes.statement: For finite χ of Gal(Φ_∞/Φ) and n≥0 through which χ factors, set δ_χ(x)=π^(−n−1)Σ_{γ∈Gal(Φ_n/Φ)}χ(γ)·δ_n(x)^γ in a finite coefficient extension of Φ. It is independent of n and satisfies δ_χ(βx)=χ(β)⁻¹δ_χ(x). In particular no n=−1 evaluation is used to define δ₁.
hypotheses: The standing BKO local datum: p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, O=O_Φ, π=−p, a Lubin–Tate O-module F for π, and the specified π-adic Tate basis and towers.
proofSteps: Differentiate the Coleman norm identity with the invariant derivation, obtaining Σ_{t∈F[π]}Dlog f(X+_F t)=πDlog f([π]X).
Evaluate on torsion to get Tr_(Φ_(n+1)/Φ_n)δ_(n+1)=πδ_n.
Use trace transitivity for level independence and reindex the character sum for inverse covariance.

sources.match: BKO define δ_χ(x)=π^(−n−1)Σ_(γ∈Gal(Φ_n/Φ))χ(γ)δ_n(x)^γ for any n through which χ factors, note independence of n, and prove δ_χ(x^β)=χ(β)⁻¹δ_χ(x). The node states the same definition with π=−p and the inverse covariance.

acceptance: Compute χ=1 at n=0 and a nonquadratic χ at n+1; the π trace factor cancels one extra π denominator and the covariance is inverse.

nodes.title: Anticyclotomic derivative descent
nodes.statement: For χ factoring through G⁻, δ_χ kills (σ−1)U_∞*, hence gives a continuous O-linear map V_∞*→Φ(χ). The map δ also descends and is Λ-linear for the augmentation action on O.

proofSteps: Apply inverse covariance with χ(σ)=1.
Use the quotient universal property, retaining uniqueness.
Use covariance at zero for the augmentation map.

sources.match: Taking β=σ∈G⁺ and χ anticyclotomic in the covariance law, BKO conclude that δ_χ vanishes on (σ−1)U*_∞ and so is defined on V*_∞. The node adds the same descent for δ.

acceptance: The descended map has the same values on x and σx, and its lift back to U_∞* is unique.

nodes.title: Trivial-character normalization
nodes.statement: On U_∞* and V_∞*, δ₁=(1−π⁻¹)δ=(1+p⁻¹)δ as Φ-valued maps. Thus δ and δ₁ have the same kernel, although δ₁ need not be O-valued.
hypotheses: The standing BKO local datum: p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, O=O_Φ, π=−p, a Lubin–Tate O-module F for π, and the specified π-adic Tate basis and towers.
proofSteps: Evaluate the invariant norm-derivative identity at zero. The π-torsion sum equals πδ; subtract the zero-torsion contribution δ.
The remaining nonzero π-torsion orbit is Tr_(Φ₀/Φ)δ₀=(π−1)δ.
Divide by π and substitute π=−p.

sources.match: BKO's definition at the trivial character and level zero gives δ₁=π⁻¹Tr_(Φ₀/Φ)δ₀; their formulas (3.6)–(3.7) differ at χ=1 exactly by the Euler factor at p, which is the relation of the node.
Rubin records δ=−(p/(p+1))δ_(χ₀) with his p^(−n−1) normalisation; with BKO's π^(−n−1)=(−p)^(−n−1) normalisation this is δ₁=(1+p⁻¹)δ.

acceptance: Keep the p-Euler-factor correction at χ=1; do not assert δ₁=δ.

nodes.title: Formal Kummer exact sequence
nodes.statement: For each finite L in Θ_∞ or Ψ_∞ and k≥1, the multiplication-by-π^k sequence on F(m_(Φ̄)) yields 0→F(m_L)/π^k→H¹(L,F[π^k])→H¹(L,F(m_(Φ̄)))[π^k]→0. These sequences commute with restriction, corestriction/formal trace and k-transition maps.
hypotheses: The standing BKO local datum: p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, O=O_Φ, π=−p, a Lubin–Tate O-module F for π, and the specified π-adic Tate basis and towers.
proofSteps: Use finite-flat torsion and divisibility over the algebraic closure, evaluated in finite complete subfields.
Take the continuous cohomology long exact sequence; identify fixed formal points with F(m_L).
Check transfer is formal-group norm and that transition maps on torsion and quotients agree.

sources.match: BKO apply Galois cohomology over Θ_n to the multiplication-by-π^(n+1) sequence on F(Φ̄) and obtain the injection of F(Θ_n)/π^(n+1) into H¹(Θ_n,F[π^(n+1)]) with cokernel the π^(n+1)-torsion of H¹(Θ_n,F(Φ̄)). The node states this for every finite layer and every k, with transfer compatibilities.
Rubin writes the same sequence with p^(n+1) in place of π^(n+1).

acceptance: Track the connecting map on an actual π^k-division point and verify that corestriction is formal trace, not coordinate addition.

nodes.title: Height-two universal norm vanishing
nodes.statement: For the totally ramified pro-p towers Θ_∞/Φ and Ψ_∞/Φ, lim_N F(m_(Θ_n))=0 and lim_N F(m_(Ψ_n))=0. Equivalently every finite-layer universal formal norm subgroup is zero.
hypotheses: The standing BKO local datum: p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, O=O_Φ, π=−p, a Lubin–Tate O-module F for π, and the specified π-adic Tate basis and towers.
proofSteps: Apply Hazewinkel Theorem 1.3 in a cofinal totally ramified Z_p direction and use transitivity/containment for the full two-variable tower.
For a fixed ramified finite layer, use the ramified-base version of the height-two norm bound stated by Rubin Proposition 4.5; a depth tending to infinity forces the intersection to zero.

Use separatedness of the local-field filtration. Record the precise ramified-base estimate as gap G1 until its proof is supplied; the absolutely unramified base case alone does not prove every inverse-limit coordinate zero. A lead for G1: Θ_∞ and Ψ_∞ are deeply ramified, and deeply ramified theory gives the direct-limit Kummer defect vanishing of formal-kummer-duality directly (see the G1 record).
